title: How do we place a protractor and read the angle?
description: The centre of the protractor goes on the vertex, one arm lies along the zero, and the angle is read on the set of numbers that starts at that zero. Keeko's doubt, that the outer set gives one hundred degrees, is broken by showing that the outer set starts from the other arm.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the set whose zero lies on the base arm. Watch for children who read the nearer or the larger number without checking where the zero is.

source: Place the protractor so the centre is on the vertex of the a
video_script.why: The child learns the steps of placing a protractor and reading the set of numbers that starts at zero on the base arm.
video_script.substitution: The zero of a protractor is used like the zero of a ruler: it is put on the start of what is measured.
video_script.anchor: the book's picture of a protractor on the angle AOB, with the arm OB along the base on the right-hand zero
video_script.wrong_answer: read the outer scale, so the angle is one hundred degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the outer scale and says the angle is one hundred degrees. The outer zero is on the other side, away from the base arm, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The angle eigh oh bee measures eighty degrees

final_answer.spoken: angle eigh oh bee is eighty degrees

maths_rules: ground: the zero of a ruler goes at the start of what is measured; the zero of the protractor goes on one arm of the angle
centre of the protractor on the vertex O; arm OB along the base line on the right-hand 0 of the inner set
the inner set starts at 0 on OB; the arm OA passes through 80, so angle AOB = 80 degrees
check: the angle is smaller than a right angle, and 80 is smaller than 90
the outer set starts at 0 on the other side, and reads 180 - 80 = 100 where OA crosses; this is not the angle AOB
video_script.design: The protractor stays on the angle all video. The inner set is lit teal and the outer set amber. The outer reading of 100 appears only in Keeko's doubt.
